summary.note_test_i: On a stereotyped 1D VR track, laps are nearly identical trajectories, so pre/post occupancy (position x speed) is already nearly matched. The model therefore PREDICTS attenuation A ~ small here, unlike in the open field where marginal occupancy matching removed most of the naive sampling bias. A small A in this dataset is consistent with the model, not evidence against occupancy confounds in 2D.
summary.note_attenuation: The per-session attenuation index A = 1 - delta_matched/delta_raw is ill-conditioned whenever delta_raw ~ 0 (which is itself the predicted outcome on stereotyped laps); prefer attenuation_pooled = 1 - mean(delta_matched)/mean(delta_raw) and the paired raw-vs-matched Wilcoxon.
summary.note_matching: Caveat discovered during matching: pre vs post speed distributions differ most near the reward zones (anticipatory slowing at the NEW zone appears only post-switch), so (position-bin x speed-tercile) min-count matching leaves almost no frames precisely there (see n_lowocc_bins_*). Without an occupancy floor, near-zero-occupancy bins produce spuriously high rate estimates and artifactual 'toward-reward' matched shifts (e.g. m11 ses-05: delta_matched -0.14 without floor vs -0.04 with a 1-s floor). Aggregate maps therefore NaN bins with < OCC_FLOOR_S seconds of occupancy per condition and interpolate them circularly. This is a structural limitation of marginal occupancy matching on tasks where behaviour covaries with the variable of interest at the measurement location.

prediction4_lick_before_map.caveat: map latency is lower-bounded at 5 trials by the minimum sliding-window size
